jobs.description:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

The Core AI Model Training team leads research and engineering across the full lifecycle of large language model development for enterprise use cases including data curation pretraining fine tuning and evaluation. Our goal is to continuously improve our custom enterprise models by incorporating novel techniques and optimizing training and inference efficiency establishing a differentiated advantage for AI applications across the platform.

These models are consumed across multiple business units to power a wide range of use cases enabling teams to solve complex problems and deliver tailored solutions. You'll help build the next generation of enterprise language models that bring AI experiences into our customers' day to day work serving more than 9000 enterprise customers worldwide. We're just getting started with our early adopter customers and we need your help building an amazing range of solutions.

What You Get To Do In This Role

Confronted with real world challenges and datasets you will use your AI and ML expertise and creativity to apply existing methods and develop new ones to solve problems in a practical and scalable way.
Research propose implement train and evaluate models and techniques end to end.
Build and maintain training pipelines and evaluation harnesses that make results reproducible and progress measurable.
Collaborate daily with research scientists engineers and product managers to ship high quality high impact work.
Own your work from design through implementation testing and delivery partnering with product owners to translate requirements into results.

Qualifications

Expertise in LLM post training including supervised fine tuning and distillation.
Expertise in reinforcement learning for LLMs including PPO GRPO DPO and reward modeling.
Hands on experience with training frameworks and distributed and large scale training including FSDP DeepSpeed and Megatron as well as parallelism strategies such as tensor pipeline expert and data parallelism.
Experience with synthetic data generation for training and evaluation.
Experience with data curation at scale including deduplication filtering and data mixture design.
Familiarity with a range of transformer architectures including decoder only or autoregressive encoder decoder and mixture of experts.
Expert level Python with strong OOP and design pattern fundamentals.
Ability to read current research and rapidly prototype and experiment with new ideas.
3 or more years of relevant experience with a Bachelor's degree 3 or more years with a Master's degree a PhD or equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications

Grounding in evaluation and benchmarking including building evaluation harnesses contamination checks and custom enterprise benchmarks.
Pretraining experience or an end to end perspective across pretraining and post training with an understanding of how choices in one stage propagate to the other.
Familiarity with inference and serving technologies such as vLLM or SGLang quantization and KV cache tradeoffs.
Publications at top tier venues such as ICLR NeurIPS ICML ACL EMNLP or AAAI.
Fluency with AI productivity tools such as Claude Code and Codex with a track record of thoughtfully integrating AI into engineering and research workflows.

jobs.description:
Company Description

It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive
. As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery
and minimally invasive care
, our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system
and Ion
—have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.

We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.

The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.

If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare
, you’ll find your purpose here.

Job Description

Primary Function of Position

The Senior Clinical Data Scientist will be part of the Ion business unit. The Ion endoluminal system is Intuitive's robotic platform for minimally invasive biopsy in the peripheral lung, with an initial goal of improving the early diagnosis of lung cancer. The Senior Clinical Data Scientist sits at the intersection of clinical science and data science within the Ion business unit, translating clinical questions into rigorous, data-driven analyses that inform product strategy, evidence generation, and business decisions. This role reports to the Managing Staff, Clinical Data Science.

The individual in this role will partner with clinicians, cross-functional teams, and data engineering to design and execute a clinical data science strategy — defining hypotheses grounded in customer needs, identifying appropriate data sources, conducting quantitative analyses, and communicating results that demonstrably impact patient outcomes and business objectives. Unlike a purely clinical or purely technical role, this position demands both deep clinical understanding of the Ion platform and hands-on proficiency in modern data science methods and tools.

Success requires a strong technical foundation in Python or R, statistics, and causal reasoning; the ability to navigate ambiguity in a fast-evolving clinical and commercial landscape; and exceptional skill in communicating complex findings clearly — especially through polished visual presentations and well-organized documentation.

Essential Job Duties

Work with internal and external stakeholders (including clinicians, administrators, and policymakers) to identify data-centric needs in the clinical space and translate them into prioritized research questions with testable hypotheses.
Design, implement, and validate quantitative analyses in Python or R — applying appropriate statistical, machine learning, and causal inference methods to Ion device logs, clinical studies/registries, insurance claims databases, and EHR/EMR data — to test hypotheses.
Translate analyses into decision-useful stories, tailoring them to diverse groups of stakeholders — from technical peers building product, to senior leadership defining strategy, to external physicians looking to improve efficiency.
Demonstrate impact through internal/external reports, presentations, dashboards, peer-reviewed publications, and customer-facing deliverables.
Partner with cross-functional teams to assist with the design and execution of global clinical and economic evidence strategies, including designing and supporting clinical trials.
Support regulatory submissions by structuring and validating clinical datasets to meet FDA and EU MDR compliance standards.
Create and maintain well-organized, reproducible codebases with clear documentation, version control, and consistent coding standards.
Catalyze a data-driven culture internally — champion the use of data to generate compelling evidence and ultimately build a better product.

Qualifications

Required Skills and Experience

6+ years of experience with Master's degree or 4+ years with PhD in a quantitative, scientific, or engineering field (e.g., biostatistics, epidemiology, data science, computer science, biomedical engineering, public health, or a related discipline). MD with quantitative research experience also accepted.
Experience with Python or R for data analysis, statistical modeling, and visualization.
Working knowledge of SQL for querying and managing structured datasets.
Demonstrated experience with causal inference methods and study design.
Experience working with device-generated log data, clinical study/registry data, and claims/EHR-style databases.
Experience with causal inference in a healthcare or medical device context.
Experience using platforms such as Snowflake or Databricks for production-level data pipelines and analytics.
Experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau) for the presentation of complex data to non-technical stakeholders or regulatory bodies.
Experience with Electronic Data Capture (EDC) systems (e.g., Medrio) for managing clinical study/registry data.
Experience using AI/ML tools to accelerate software development and data analysis workflows.

Preferred Skills And Experience

Excellent critical thinking and analytical skills, with the ability to frame ambiguous clinical questions as testable hypotheses and select fit-for-purpose methods.
Stellar organizational skills, particularly with respect to code management and documentation.
Ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams, including clinicians, engineers, regulatory, commercial, and data science partners.
Self-starter attitude with the ability to manage multiple priorities, operate independently, and deliver under ambiguity.
Track record of peer-reviewed publications or conference presentations in clinical research or data science.
Experience in medical devices or other regulated industries.
Familiarity with Good Clinical Practice (GCP), ISO 14155 (clinical investigation of medical devices), and data privacy regulations (HIPAA/GDPR).
Familiarity with the lung cancer landscape (screening, diagnosis, treatment).

jobs.description:
Job Details

Job Description:

About Central Engineering Group — Networking Architecture

The CEG Networking Architecture Group defines next-generation networking silicon and platform architecture for hyperscale data centers, cloud infrastructure, and AI workloads. The team focuses on IPU/DPU platforms, advanced packet processing, programmable networking, and the data-movement technologies that enable modern distributed computing systems to scale efficiently.

Position Overview

This role is for a senior AI systems architect who can translate the communication, memory, and orchestration bottlenecks of large-scale AI into networking architecture, IP, and platform direction. The successful candidate will work across research, architecture, silicon, software, and product teams to shape the next generation of distributed AI infrastructure.

As a Senior AI Architect/Researcher, you will help define how AI systems communicate and move data at scale across xPUs, DPUs, IPUs, NICs, memory, and heterogeneous storage. In this pathfinding and research role, you will advance new architectural approaches and translate research insights into network architecture and software capabilities that can influence N+1 to N+3 product roadmap.

The ideal candidate thinks in systems rather than components, understands the memory wall and scale-out serving bottlenecks, and can reason across interconnect, memory hierarchy, software runtime, and compute to unlock the next order of magnitude in AI efficiency. You will help set technical direction and influence silicon and software roadmaps. The candidate is expected to maintain substantial knowledge of state-of-the-art principles and theories, contribute regularly to scientific literature and the research community-at-large, and may participate in the development of Intellectual Property.

Key Responsibilities

Turn Workload Analysis into New IP

Analyze real AI serving and training workloads, identify communication and memory bottlenecks, and translate those findings into new IP, offload engines, platform features, and architecture requirements
Drive hardware-software co-design across compute, DPU/IPU, NIC, SoC fabric, and AI serving runtimes, ensuring that networking and data-movement capabilities are reflected in modern inference and training frameworks such as vLLM, SGLang, and others

Architect AI-Scale Networking and Interconnect

Define the architectural direction for how AI systems and infrastructure move data at scale across xPU-to-xPU, xPU-to-storage, and cross-node paths spanning IPU/DPU platforms, NICs, and heterogeneous storage
Shape next-generation packet processing, RDMA-class transport, and programmable networking IP that forms the backbone of hyperscale AI inference and training

Attack the Memory Wall and System-Level Bottlenecks

Investigate the fundamental data-movement bottlenecks in large-scale AI and Agentic inference and training, including KV-cache transfer, disaggregated prefill/decode, model and tensor parallelism, and communication collectives, and translate them into concrete architectural requirements
Reason across the full memory hierarchy and interconnect to minimize copies, latency, and bandwidth overhead, balancing latency-sensitive control paths against bandwidth-intensive data-paths

Set Roadmap and Lead Across Teams

Shape multi-generation compute, memory, and interconnect roadmaps across IPU/DPU product lines by defining scaling strategies, migration paths, and architecture requirements that connect research insights to product execution
Align architecture across networking, SoC fabric, firmware/OS/drivers, and performance modeling teams

What We're Looking For

To be successful in this role, you should demonstrate the following professional traits:

Architectural vision — defines long-term strategy across AI systems, networking, memory, and software domains
Influence without authority — drives alignment across multiple teams and disciplines
Systems thinking — understands interactions across compute, memory, network, and software
Decision-making under ambiguity — makes sound tradeoffs with incomplete data
Collaboration — builds strong cross-functional relationships
Customer-oriented mindset — translates workload needs into architectural innovations
Ownership and accountability — drives initiatives end-to-end
Continuous learning — stays current with evolving AI systems, inference runtimes, interconnects, memory technologies, and cloud infrastructure trends

A strong candidate will have enough depth to reason from first principles, enough practical experience to understand implementation constraints, and enough leadership range to align research, architecture, software, and silicon teams around a coherent direction.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related STEM field with 5+ years of relevant experience; or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related STEM field with 2+ years of relevant experience

The Experience Must Include

Experience with modern AI training and/or inference systems, including model architecture internals, hardware algorithm code design, serving runtimes, and the memory and data-movement bottlenecks that govern large-scale performance
Hands-on experience with modern inference and training serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang, and others, with practical understanding of disaggregated prefill/decode, model parallelism, tensor parallelism, and the communication patterns they create
Experience in computer architecture and system-level design, with a focus on networking, interconnect, or memory subsystems
Proficiency in C/C++ and/or Python

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with memory hierarchy and system bottleneck analysis, including caches, memory controllers, bandwidth/latency tradeoffs, and the memory wall as it applies to data-intensive workloads
High-performance networking and data-movement technologies such as RDMA/RoCE, InfiniBand, or equivalent transport and interconnect
Experience with IPU/DPU/SmartNIC or accelerator-centric SoCs, particularly in cloud and hyperscale environments
Familiarity with PCIe, CXL, and memory semantics for high-performance IO
Experience defining architecture from concept through silicon, platform software, or shipping product, including translating workload analysis into architecture requirements and new IP
Track record of cross-team technical leadership and influencing architecture and roadmap at a senior level

jobs.description:
About Lightfield

Lightfield is reimagining CRM as a world model of a business. By learning from emails, meetings, and customer conversations, we’re building a living understanding of how a company works—so AI can help teams anticipate what comes next, make better decisions, and take action.

More than 5,000 companies have used the product since its November launch. We’ve raised more than $70M from Andreessen Horowitz, Coatue, Maverick Ventures, and Greylock to attack the biggest software category in the world. We previously built Tome, which reached more than 25 million users, and our team brings experience from Llama, Instagram, Google, and Salesforce.

About The Role

We’re starting Lightfield Research to build a Business World Model through frontier research in simulation, world modeling and self-improvement. We’re hiring applied researchers and research scientists to lead its first projects.

You’ll report directly to Ves Stoyanov, co-founder and Chief AI Officer, previously at Facebook AI, where he co-authored RoBERTa and XLM-R. You’ll work alongside AI engineers who take research into production and GTM experts who help define tasks and quality.

Researchers at Lightfield own projects from the first question through measurable product impact and publication. You’ll help shape the lab’s research agenda, culture and reputation as it grows.

What you’ll do

Lead research projects in evaluation, benchmarks, deal prediction, simulation and self-improvement.
Design empirical evaluations of Lightfield’s AI system using LLM-as-judge, rubric-based grading, offline replay and A/B tests, on both production and offline data.
Build benchmarks for core GTM tasks such as list building, CSV imports, mail intelligence, record updates and outbound. Measure Lightfield against frontier models and competitors.
Build simulated companies with users and streams of email, meetings and knowledge, where the right answers are known. Use them to evaluate the full system end to end.
Develop techniques that let Lightfield improve as it operates, at the world, company and user levels. These include reinforcement learning and, where it pays off, fine-tuning.
Model deal probability and the factors behind it, and ship them as product features.
Improve cost and quality trade-offs across the AI system, including inference cost.
Publish research blog posts, open benchmarks, arXiv reports and papers, and present at conferences and meetups.
Help build a world-class research team by recruiting and mentoring teammates.

Who you are

You have 7+ years of applied research experience in ML or NLP, in industry or academia.
You have a PhD or MS in Computer Science, Machine Learning or a related field, or equivalent research experience.
You have a track record of research that shipped or was published: papers, open-source models, datasets or benchmarks.
You have deep hands-on experience with LLMs, including evaluation, agent design and retrieval. Post-training experience (SFT, RL, preference optimization) is a plus.
You are rigorous about experimental design and can tell a real improvement from noise.
You write strong Python and are comfortable working in a production codebase (TypeScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL) alongside engineers.
You can drive an ambiguous problem independently and balance ambitious goals with frequent, visible results.
You communicate clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, in writing and in talks.
You are energized by building AI that businesses depend on to do their jobs.

Nice to have

Experience building simulations, synthetic data or RL environments.
Experience with forecasting or predictive modeling on business data.
Experience creating benchmarks adopted by others.

The Position

Forward Deployed Engineers sit inside the client’s problem, not next to it. You embed with an enterprise team, find the work that actually warrants AI, architect the system, build it, and make it hold up in the real environment.

This is a three-way role: consultant, operator, engineer
. You should be as comfortable pressure-testing a business case with a COO or VP of Engineering as you are debugging why an agent’s tool-calling loop degraded after a context change. The people who succeed here can hold a discovery conversation on Monday and ship what they scoped on Thursday.

On this track, your edge is application engineering: you make agents real inside the client’s actual systems, workflows, and delivery pipelines.

We work with regulated industries and Fortune 500 clients who have AI mandates, real constraints, and low tolerance for demos that don’t hold up.

How We Approach The Work

FDEs are trusted to shape the solution, not only deliver it. Every engagement calls for architect-level judgment:

Reframes the request. Treats “we need an agent for X” as a hypothesis, not a spec.
Decomposes the problem. Outcome → process → decisions → data → systems → actors → constraints — before choosing technology.
Chooses the intervention. Remove, simplify, traditional software, automation, LLM, RAG, agent, or multi-agent — and defends why.
Owns the architecture decision. Documents trade-offs (ADRs), sets success metrics, pushes back on scope that won’t deliver value.

Consultative Discovery

Clients rarely arrive with a fully formed problem, and the FDE’s first contribution is helping them see it clearly. You lead discovery with genuine curiosity, moving the conversation from stated requirements to underlying needs, and you build credibility through the depth of your understanding rather than the breadth of your pitch.

Uncovers business drivers. What outcome matters, what it’s worth, why now, and what happens if nothing changes.
Uncovers personal drivers. What each stakeholder is measured on, what they’re worried about, and what a win looks like for them individually.
Surfaces constraints early. Security, compliance, data access, budget, skills, politics, timelines — the things that kill projects in month two.
Aligns stakeholders. Spots conflicting goals between business, engineering, and risk, and brings them to a shared definition of success.
Asks strategic questions. Follows the answer with “why,” “how do you know,” and “what happens today when…” — without interrogating. Clients leave the conversation understanding their own problem better.

Job Description

Primary Function of Position

The Senior Clinical Data Scientist will be part of the Ion business unit. The Ion endoluminal system is Intuitive's robotic platform for minimally invasive biopsy in the peripheral lung, with an initial goal of improving the early diagnosis of lung cancer. The Senior Clinical Data Scientist sits at the intersection of clinical science and data science within the Ion business unit, translating clinical questions into rigorous, data-driven analyses that inform product strategy, evidence generation, and business decisions. This role reports to the Managing Staff, Clinical Data Science.

The individual in this role will partner with clinicians, cross-functional teams, and data engineering to design and execute a clinical data science strategy — defining hypotheses grounded in customer needs, identifying appropriate data sources, conducting quantitative analyses, and communicating results that demonstrably impact patient outcomes and business objectives. Unlike a purely clinical or purely technical role, this position demands both deep clinical understanding of the Ion platform and hands-on proficiency in modern data science methods and tools.

Success requires a strong technical foundation in Python or R, statistics, and causal reasoning; the ability to navigate ambiguity in a fast-evolving clinical and commercial landscape; and exceptional skill in communicating complex findings clearly — especially through polished visual presentations and well-organized documentation.

Work with internal and external stakeholders (including clinicians, administrators, and policymakers) to identify data-centric needs in the clinical space and translate them into prioritized research questions with testable hypotheses.
Design, implement, and validate quantitative analyses in Python or R — applying appropriate statistical, machine learning, and causal inference methods to Ion device logs, clinical studies/registries, insurance claims databases, and EHR/EMR data — to test hypotheses.
Translate analyses into decision-useful stories, tailoring them to diverse groups of stakeholders — from technical peers building product, to senior leadership defining strategy, to external physicians looking to improve efficiency.

Job Description:

About Central Engineering Group — Networking Architecture

The CEG Networking Architecture Group defines next-generation networking silicon and platform architecture for hyperscale data centers, cloud infrastructure, and AI workloads. The team focuses on IPU/DPU platforms, advanced packet processing, programmable networking, and the data-movement technologies that enable modern distributed computing systems to scale efficiently.

Position Overview

This role is for a senior AI systems architect who can translate the communication, memory, and orchestration bottlenecks of large-scale AI into networking architecture, IP, and platform direction. The successful candidate will work across research, architecture, silicon, software, and product teams to shape the next generation of distributed AI infrastructure.

As a Senior AI Architect/Researcher, you will help define how AI systems communicate and move data at scale across xPUs, DPUs, IPUs, NICs, memory, and heterogeneous storage. In this pathfinding and research role, you will advance new architectural approaches and translate research insights into network architecture and software capabilities that can influence N+1 to N+3 product roadmap.

The ideal candidate thinks in systems rather than components, understands the memory wall and scale-out serving bottlenecks, and can reason across interconnect, memory hierarchy, software runtime, and compute to unlock the next order of magnitude in AI efficiency. You will help set technical direction and influence silicon and software roadmaps. The candidate is expected to maintain substantial knowledge of state-of-the-art principles and theories, contribute regularly to scientific literature and the research community-at-large, and may participate in the development of Intellectual Property.

Key Responsibilities

Turn Workload Analysis into New IP

Analyze real AI serving and training workloads, identify communication and memory bottlenecks, and translate those findings into new IP, offload engines, platform features, and architecture requirements
Drive hardware-software co-design across compute, DPU/IPU, NIC, SoC fabric, and AI serving runtimes, ensuring that networking and data-movement capabilities are reflected in modern inference and training frameworks such as vLLM, SGLang, and others

Architect AI-Scale Networking and Interconnect

Define the architectural direction for how AI systems and infrastructure move data at scale across xPU-to-xPU, xPU-to-storage, and cross-node paths spanning IPU/DPU platforms, NICs, and heterogeneous storage
Shape next-generation packet processing, RDMA-class transport, and programmable networking IP that forms the backbone of hyperscale AI inference and training

Attack the Memory Wall and System-Level Bottlenecks

Investigate the fundamental data-movement bottlenecks in large-scale AI and Agentic inference and training, including KV-cache transfer, disaggregated prefill/decode, model and tensor parallelism, and communication collectives, and translate them into concrete architectural requirements
Reason across the full memory hierarchy and interconnect to minimize copies, latency, and bandwidth overhead, balancing latency-sensitive control paths against bandwidth-intensive data-paths

Set Roadmap and Lead Across Teams

Shape multi-generation compute, memory, and interconnect roadmaps across IPU/DPU product lines by defining scaling strategies, migration paths, and architecture requirements that connect research insights to product execution
Align architecture across networking, SoC fabric, firmware/OS/drivers, and performance modeling teams

Architectural vision — defines long-term strategy across AI systems, networking, memory, and software domains

Systems thinking — understands interactions across compute, memory, network, and software
Decision-making under ambiguity — makes sound tradeoffs with incomplete data
Collaboration — builds strong cross-functional relationships
Customer-oriented mindset — translates workload needs into architectural innovations
Ownership and accountability — drives initiatives end-to-end
Continuous learning — stays current with evolving AI systems, inference runtimes, interconnects, memory technologies, and cloud infrastructure trends

Minimum Qualifications

Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related STEM field with 5+ years of relevant experience; or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related STEM field with 2+ years of relevant experience

The Experience Must Include

Experience with modern AI training and/or inference systems, including model architecture internals, hardware algorithm code design, serving runtimes, and the memory and data-movement bottlenecks that govern large-scale performance
Hands-on experience with modern inference and training serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang, and others, with practical understanding of disaggregated prefill/decode, model parallelism, tensor parallelism, and the communication patterns they create
Experience in computer architecture and system-level design, with a focus on networking, interconnect, or memory subsystems
Proficiency in C/C++ and/or Python

High-performance networking and data-movement technologies such as RDMA/RoCE, InfiniBand, or equivalent transport and interconnect
Experience with IPU/DPU/SmartNIC or accelerator-centric SoCs, particularly in cloud and hyperscale environments

About The Role

We’re starting Lightfield Research to build a Business World Model through frontier research in simulation, world modeling and self-improvement. We’re hiring applied researchers and research scientists to lead its first projects.

You’ll report directly to Ves Stoyanov, co-founder and Chief AI Officer, previously at Facebook AI, where he co-authored RoBERTa and XLM-R. You’ll work alongside AI engineers who take research into production and GTM experts who help define tasks and quality.

Researchers at Lightfield own projects from the first question through measurable product impact and publication. You’ll help shape the lab’s research agenda, culture and reputation as it grows.

What you’ll do

Lead research projects in evaluation, benchmarks, deal prediction, simulation and self-improvement.
Design empirical evaluations of Lightfield’s AI system using LLM-as-judge, rubric-based grading, offline replay and A/B tests, on both production and offline data.
Build benchmarks for core GTM tasks such as list building, CSV imports, mail intelligence, record updates and outbound. Measure Lightfield against frontier models and competitors.
Build simulated companies with users and streams of email, meetings and knowledge, where the right answers are known. Use them to evaluate the full system end to end.
Develop techniques that let Lightfield improve as it operates, at the world, company and user levels. These include reinforcement learning and, where it pays off, fine-tuning.
Model deal probability and the factors behind it, and ship them as product features.
Improve cost and quality trade-offs across the AI system, including inference cost.
Publish research blog posts, open benchmarks, arXiv reports and papers, and present at conferences and meetups.
Help build a world-class research team by recruiting and mentoring teammates.

Who you are

You have 7+ years of applied research experience in ML or NLP, in industry or academia.
You have a PhD or MS in Computer Science, Machine Learning or a related field, or equivalent research experience.
You have a track record of research that shipped or was published: papers, open-source models, datasets or benchmarks.

You can drive an ambiguous problem independently and balance ambitious goals with frequent, visible results.
You communicate clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, in writing and in talks.
You are energized by building AI that businesses depend on to do their jobs.

Experience building simulations, synthetic data or RL environments.

Experience creating benchmarks adopted by others.

new_jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, GPU Code Generation for Machine Learning Inference
new_jobs.description:
NVIDIA is seeking talented engineers to join the TensorRT team and advance high-performance AI inference on NVIDIA GPUs. Our team develops software that accelerates state-of-the-art generative AI models for local and enterprise deployments. We solve challenging problems in GPU code generation, just-in-time compilation, and inference optimization to deliver high performance across diverse models and hardware configurations.

As a Senior Software Engineer, you will develop advanced GPU inference software for TensorRT. We’re looking for engineers with strong experience in GPU optimization and compiler development who can translate a deep understanding of GPU execution into efficient code generation and measurable improvements in generative AI inference.

What You’ll Be Doing

Design and implement efficient GPU code generation techniques in TensorRT that balance generated code performance, compilation overhead, and startup latency.
Develop compiler optimizations, including operator fusion, dynamic scheduling, and specialization for model shapes, data types, and GPU architectures.
Profile workloads and analyze generated GPU code to identify bottlenecks and guide compiler and runtime improvements.
Develop robust, maintainable software in C++, and Python for tooling, testing, and performance analysis.
Collaborate with GPU architects, kernel developers, compiler engineers, and deep learning experts to guide hardware and software design.

What We Need To See

BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
4+ years of relevant software development experience, including contributions to a substantial codebase or project.
Strong proficiency in C++ and experience building performance-critical software.
Understanding of GPU architecture and parallel programming concepts, including memory hierarchies, thread execution, synchronization, and resource utilization.
A rigorous approach to performance analysis and debugging, with the ability to validate numerical correctness and explain performance tradeoffs.
Strong problem-solving and communication skills, and the ability to work independently and collaborate across teams.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Experience developing or optimizing GPU kernels using CUDA, Triton, CuTe DSL, CUTLASS, or other GPU programming languages.
Experience with MLIR compiler infrastructure, familiarity with intermediate representations, lowering, optimization passes, and GPU code generation.
Familiarity with NVIDIA Tensor Core architecture, mixed-precision computation, quantization, or low-level GPU performance analysis using tools such as NVIDIA Nsight.
Experience developing inference frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, and SGLang.
A track record of measurable performance improvements in production software or contributions to GPU programming and compiler projects.

At NVIDIA, you’ll work with engineers across GPU architecture, compilers, and AI software to solve demanding performance problems. If you are curious and enjoy understanding how hardware executes code and building software that pushes its capabilities, join us in shaping the future of generative AI inference.

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 152,000 USD - 241,500 USD for Level 3, and 184,000 USD - 287,500 USD for Level 4.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.
